body_markdown:
I began writing about the[interesting vehicles I find in car graveyards](https://www.murileemartin.com/JunkyardGalleryHome.html) nearly 20 years ago, and this is the my 3389th such article since the first one went up in early 2007. Out of all of those cars and trucks (plus[one tank](https://www.thetruthaboutcars.com/2019/09/junkyard-find-1970-alvis-combat-vehicle-reconnaissance-tracked/) ), today’s FPS entry is the oldest.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


I’ve seen plenty of older machinery in junkyards, of course, but they must be recognizable and reasonably complete to qualify as the subject of one of my articles. Prior to today’s Ford,[this 1937 Hudson Terraplane near Denver](https://www.autoblog.com/features/junkyard-gem-1937-hudson-terraplane/) was the earliest such vehicle.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


This[1938 Oldsmobile Eight in Wyoming](https://www.thetruthaboutcars.com/cars/down-on-the-junkyard/junkyard-find-1938-oldsmobile-touring-sedan-44496621) was one year newer.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


Also a 1938 model,[this Ford De Luxe Tudor](https://www.autoblog.com/news/junkyard-gem-1938-ford-tudor/) resides in the very same Colorado yard as today’s Final Parking Space entrant.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


That yard is[Speedway Auto Wrecking in Dacono](https://murileemartin.substack.com/p/gm-and-chrysler-iron-at-colorados) , which has a vast stockpile of 1930s-1980s American vehicles. We’ve seen some interesting cars and trucks at Speedway in this series, including a[1942 GMC CCKW](https://www.hagerty.com/media/opinion/final-parking-space/final-parking-space-1942-gmc-cckw-deuce-and-a-half/) “Deuce and a Half,” an[ex-military IHC Metro-Mite](https://www.hagerty.com/media/opinion/final-parking-space/final-parking-space-international-harvester-metro-mite/) , a[1965 Dodge Dart wagon](https://www.hagerty.com/media/opinion/final-parking-space/final-parking-space-1965-dodge-dart-170-wagon/) , and a[1946 Pontiac Streamliner](https://www.hagerty.com/media/opinion/final-parking-space/final-parking-space-1946-pontiac-streamliner-4-door-sedan/) . If you decide to visit, be aware that business hours are Saturday mornings only.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


This truck’s final parking space ended up being next to a genuine[Austin FX3](https://www.hagerty.com/media/market-trends/austin-london-cab/) , best known as the immediate predecessor to the famous[Austin FX4 London Black Cab](https://www.hagerty.com/media/automotive-history/taxi-the-origin-of-londons-black-cabs/) .


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


This old Brit could tell some stories.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


What always catches my eye about this truck are the weathered “RARIN’ TO GO” logos painted on the doors.


Unknown


That’s the logo of Frontier Gas, the gasoline brand created by[the Frontier Refining Company of Cheyenne, Wyoming](https://www.wyohistory.org/encyclopedia/cheyennes-100-octane-aviation-fuel-plant) . Frontier expanded greatly by[refining high-octane aviation gasoline during World War II](https://cowboystatedaily.com/2025/08/31/wyoming-history-how-two-oil-refineries-fueled-u-s-wwii-aviation-dominance/) (there was and is plenty of oil drilling in northeastern Colorado and southeastern Wyoming). After the war and during a succession of corporate owners at least into the 1960s, the[Frontier Gas brand and its distinctive slogan were seen](https://www.collectorsweekly.com/stories/328080-frontier-sign-history?in=all) at service stations in Wyoming, Colorado, and adjacent states.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


This part of Speedway’s inventory is quite remote, requiring an arduous hike to the far eastern edge of the property. I like to[shoot photos with my old film cameras](https://murileemartin.substack.com/t/film-photography) in the area near today’s FPS truck; this photo was[taken with infrared film in a 1977 Canon AE-1](https://murileemartin.substack.com/p/more-fun-with-weird-film-at-speedway) .


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


I kept meaning to write a proper junkyard article about this truck, and today is the day.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


I think it was used for installing and maintaining the RARIN’ TO GO signs on all those gas stations, with some light towing duty mixed in when needed.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


I’m no expert on prewar Ford trucks, and I suspect this one is a mashup of several vehicles. I couldn’t find any serial numbers and the grille surround is long gone, but my best model-year guess from studying the cab and interior is going to be 1936.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


That makes it a[Model 67](https://www.hagerty.com/valuation-tools/past-sales/1936-ford-model_67/182830455/cb132392-64fd-4e2c-858b-a5bc2321924d) or 51, depending on whether it was a pickup that was modified for crane use after purchase (67) or began life as a cab-and-chassis platform (51) for build-it-yourself buyers. If you’re an expert on these trucks, please share your knowledge with us in the comments.


Ford Motor Company of Australia


The 1936 Ford pickups had mandatory V-8 engines in the United States (the right-hand-drive trucks in the brochure pages above are Australian-market trucks).


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


This truck has a[good old flathead V-8](https://www.hagerty.com/media/automotive-history/fords-flathead-v-8-gave-power-to-the-people/) , naturally, one of[15 million built](https://www.hagerty.com/media/automotive-history/by-the-numbers-how-ford-built-15-million-flatheads/) . No Windsor swap here!


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


That may be because it was parked for good before Ford even started building Windsor engines. These Firestone “Gum-Dipped Rayon” tires appear to date from the 1950s at the latest.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


The 59A-B code on the cylinder head tells us that this is a[postwar 239-cubic-inch engine](https://oldcarbrochures.org/United%20States/Mercury/1946_Mercury/1946-Mercury-Brochure/slides/1946_Mercury-16.html) , not the original 221. Was it the first engine swap or the fifth? We’ll never know.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


The winch is driven by a finger-removing exposed-chain-drive PTO, real school-of-hard-knocks machinery.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


There’s a lot of antique iron and steel here.


“The Ford V8 pickup for 1936 is headed for *new triumphs* .” This narrator’s enunciation skills are impressive.
